symbol_descriptions: Magnitude of the radial electric field in volts per meter
Radial distance from the finite-sized charged source center to the observation point along the normal toward the boundary in meters
Homogeneous medium permittivity for that trial in farads per meter
Perpendicular distance from the source charge center to an infinite grounded conducting plane in meters
Baseline effective source-size regularization length representing the finite spatial extent of the charged object in meters
Dimensionless anisotropic-shape saturation strength controlling how the effective normal-direction softening departs from the isotropic value near the source and near its image

Dimensionless crossover-sharpening parameter that modulates the near-field activation strength of the anisotropic softening and allows a more abrupt static polarization-induced transition to the far-field form

new_symbol_range_suggestions.gamma: gamma >= 0 and typically gamma = O(1); activation is most visible when r/a = O(1) or (2*d - r)/a = O(1), while gamma -> 0 recovers the parent

derivation_notes: The parent's single exponential crossover in the finite-size anisotropic regularization is replaced by a multiplicatively modulated crossover factor, (1 - exp(-x/a))*(1 + gamma*exp(-x/a)), which sharpens the turn-on near x=O(a) while preserving the same far-field Coulomb/image limit. The same refined static law is applied symmetrically to the real-charge and image-charge kernels because both arise from the same finite-object polarization mechanism near the grounded plane.
change_summary: I relaxed the assumption that anisotropic softening must follow one fixed exponential crossover shape. A new fixed parameter gamma sharpens the near-field crossover, changing the curvature of E(r) for r=O(a) or 2*d-r=O(a) while reducing exactly to the parent when gamma=0.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The effective normal-direction softening departs from the isotropic value with a single fixed exponential crossover in x/a for both kernels.
assumption_audit.mechanism: A finite charged object near a conductor can exhibit a more abrupt but still static polarization-induced crossover between strongly regularized near field and Coulombic far field than a single exponential captures.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting gamma = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly; the child also approaches the same Coulomb/image law when r>>a and 2*d-r>>a.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed q, d, a, beta, and epsilon_0, the target is the difference of two identically softened Coulomb/image kernels, so the near-field shape is controlled by one shared saturation form a^2*(1 + beta*(1 - exp(-x/a))) for both the real charge and its image.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the parent's single exponential saturation of the anisotropic softening with a sharper crossover that better represents induced shape polarization near the conducting plane, so the effective regularization along the normal changes more abruptly with x/a while preserving the same far-field Coulomb/image limit.
response_change.observable_effect: When q and epsilon_0 are fixed and r is scanned for multiple d/a values, the near-plane profile develops a different shoulder/curvature around r=O(a) and 2*d-r=O(a); one parent parameter set with its single crossover shape cannot match both the more abrupt near-source flattening and the far-field recovery across those conditions.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when a>0 and either r=O(a) or 2*d-r=O(a), especially with a<d but not negligibly small compared with d so that both the real-charge and image-charge softened regions can be sampled.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying r at moderate d/a already reveals the softened near-field shoulder; in holdout, broader d/a variation tests whether the same sharper crossover law transfers to both the source and image branches without separate refits.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: The child should recover the parent in the limit where the refined crossover-shape parameter tends to the parent's single-exponential form, and also in the far-field regime r>>a and 2*d-r>>a where both reduce to the same Coulomb/image law.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: distance-dependent modulation of finite-size anisotropic regularization near a conducting plane
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: A finite charged object near a conductor can exhibit a more abrupt but still static polarization-induced crossover between strongly regularized near field and Coulombic far field than a single exponential captures, altering the curvature of the measured field profile without introducing new variables.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The refinement changes the functional shape of the existing regularization law through multiplicative distance-dependent modulation rather than through a coefficient rescaling. This creates a distinct near-field curvature pattern in the scored target across dimensionless distances r/a and (2*d-r)/a while preserving the same asymptotic law, which a coefficient-only correction cannot generally reproduce over multiple d/a conditions.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The effective normal-direction softening departs from the isotropic value with a single fixed exponential crossover in x/a for both kernels.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The anisotropic softening still saturates statically with distance, but its turn-on is multiplicatively sharpened near x=O(a) by a second near-field factor representing stronger polarization-induced crossover.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting gamma = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly; the child also approaches the same Coulomb/image law when r>>a and 2*d-r>>a.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Relative to the parent's one-shape crossover, the child produces a sharper shoulder in E(r) when plotted against r at fixed q, epsilon_0, a, beta, and several d values: curvature changes are localized to r/a=O(1) or (2*d-r)/a=O(1), while far from both softened regions the curves collapse back to the same Coulomb/image behavior.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot generally absorb this change because the parent has only one crossover shape, beta*(1 - exp(-x/a)), shared by both kernels. Retuning a and beta can shift the overall softening scale and amplitude, but cannot independently reproduce the child’s sharper intermediate-distance curvature together with the same near-origin regularization and far-field recovery across multiple d/a scans using one common fit.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when a>0 and either r=O(a) or 2*d-r=O(a), especially with a<d but not negligibly small compared with d so that both the real-charge and image-charge softened regions can be sampled.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying r at moderate d/a already reveals the softened near-field shoulder; in holdout, broader d/a variation tests whether the same sharper crossover law transfers to both the source and image branches without separate refits.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: The child should recover the parent in the limit where the refined crossover-shape parameter tends to the parent's single-exponential form, and also in the far-field regime r>>a and 2*d-r>>a where both reduce to the same Coulomb/image law.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes one specific exponential saturation law for how anisotropic finite-size regularization turns on with distance from both the charge and its image, which is an overly restrictive shape assumption rather than a required electrostatic consequence.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The effective normal-direction softening departs from the isotropic value with a single fixed exponential crossover in x/a for both kernels.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A finite charged object near a conductor can exhibit a more abrupt but still static polarization-induced crossover between strongly regularized near field and Coulombic far field than a single exponential captures, altering the curvature of the measured field profile without introducing new variables.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent already includes the relevant process—finite-size anisotropic smoothing near a grounded plane—but fixes its distance dependence to one exponential saturation shape. A realistic next refinement is therefore to relax that mathematical assumption rather than add a separate process. The scored target mapping changes directly: at fixed q and epsilon_0, scanning r for several fixed d values, the parent predicts one universal crossover curvature in the dimensionless coordinates r/a and (2*d-r)/a. A child with a sharper static crossover changes the slope and curvature of E(r) in the near-field region while preserving positivity-compatible decay and the same far-field limit. This is scientifically admissible when the observation region actually enters the softened zone, i.e. r=O(a) and/or 2*d-r=O(a), with a usually smaller than d so the source and image remain distinct. The contrast is not merely an auxiliary reformulation because the measured E itself changes as a function of supplied inputs. The limitation is that if all sampled distances satisfy r>>a and 2*d-r>>a, the refinement becomes effectively unobservable and the parent is recovered.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a declared condition to modulate the strength of an existing process.

scenario_text: A stationary positive point charge is placed in vacuum, and the electric-field magnitude is measured at different radial distances. The charge magnitude and observation distance are independently varied between trials. The target is the instantaneous field magnitude at the observation point. The benchmark tests geometric field dilution without material interfaces or time dependence.
